221: #### 4.4.1 Cost model
222: 
223: Housekeeping cost has two parts: a **fixed overhead per call** (~17k input tokens and ~13 s for `agy -p`) and the **payload**.
224: 
225: **Measured inputs:**
226: 
227: | Transcripts | Count | Median | Mean | Tool traffic |
228: |---|---|---|---|---|
229: | Antigravity top-level, esp32 | 45 surviving | 52k tokens | 120k tokens | 86% |
230: | Antigravity subagent, esp32 | 138 surviving | 29k tokens | 36k tokens | 90% |
231: | Claude Code, esp32 | 35 | ~47k tokens | ~98k tokens | 70% |
232: 
233: Session rates since May: ~1.4 top-level and ~7 subagent Antigravity sessions a day, and ~0.9 Claude Code sessions a day.
234: 
235: The Antigravity sizes above were measured on `transcript.jsonl`, which truncates large fields (§6.2). Untruncated sizes are larger, so the estimates below are lower bounds until P0 re-measures them from `transcript_full.jsonl`.
236: 
237: **Payload per episode, before any overhead.** Compaction keeps dialogue, reasoning and outcome excerpts, and those are 10–30% of a transcript, so compaction should reach 4× or more on Antigravity and 3× on Claude Code. Salience windows (§6.4) should roughly halve that again. A median Antigravity top-level episode then comes out as:
238: 
239: | Step | Tokens |
240: |---|---|
241: | Raw transcript | 52k |
242: | After compaction | ~13k |
243: | In salience windows, plus synopsis | ~7k |
244: 
245: **Estimates.** These rest on the stated assumptions, and P0/P1 measurements (compaction ratio, triage keep rate, B4) replace them.
246: 
247: | Workload | Estimate | Dominant cost | Levers |
248: |---|---|---|---|
249: | Backfill: surviving transcripts (~14M raw tokens) plus the PA archive (~1.2M tokens) | ~4–6M tokens one-off, throttled by the daily budget over days | Payload | Compaction, triage, salience windows, packing episodes to the 60k payload cap |
250: | Steady-state extraction, triage, reconcile and verify | ~100–200k tokens a day | Payload and overhead roughly equal | Pack a parent session with its subagents into one call; reconcile per subsystem batch |
251: | Interactive small calls (LLM brief fallback, déjà-vu tier 2, pull-tool synthesis) | ~17–20k tokens each on Gemini 3.8 Flash (~10k on Gemini 3.6 Flash; E10), ~85% of it overhead; 5–15 a day ≈ 75–250k tokens | **Fixed overhead** | Deterministic paths first; batch all pending tier-2 checks into one call per tick; use Gemini 3.6 Flash for simple stages (41% overhead reduction); per-day caps |
252: 
253: The fixed overhead matters most for the small, interactive calls, not for extraction. E10 confirmed that fixed overhead cannot be reduced with CLI flags and prefix caching is inactive across distinct calls (`cache_read_tokens = 0`), but model selection (Gemini 3.6 Flash) cuts overhead by 41%. E11 showed sequential calls hit zero rate limits due to the natural 10–14s wall-clock latency of `agy -p`.
254: 
255: **Packing targets per call:**
256: - triage: 20 episode synopses;
257: - extraction: salience windows from one or more episodes (a parent with its subagents first), up to 60k tokens;
258: - verification: 30 claims;
259: - reconciliation: one subsystem's candidates.
260: 
261: **Isolating housekeeping runs:**
262: - They run with the working directory `<data-dir>/runs/<repo-id>/`, not the repository, so workspace rules and hooks don't load. (Note: `--project` is silently ignored by `agy -p`, so isolation relies strictly on the isolated working directory and environment variables; E7).
263: - They set `REPO_MEMORY_HOUSEKEEPING=1`. Hooks inherit `agy`'s environment, so this plugin's own hooks exit immediately inside housekeeping runs.
264: - Capture excludes them by working directory URI and `REPO_MEMORY_HOUSEKEEPING=1`.
265: - `agy --continue` must never resume one (E7).
266: - **[R2]** On Claude Code, `claude -p --safe-mode --no-session-persistence` loads no plugins or hooks and writes no transcript, so there is nothing to exclude and recursion is impossible.
267: 
268: **Report conversations are captured**, but only messages a human typed count as evidence. The report's own text, and the automated kickoff prompt that started the conversation, were generated from memory, so re-extracting them would reinforce memory with itself. The mechanism is in §9.2.1.
269: 
270: ### 4.5 Components
271: 
272: | Component | Responsibility | Invoked by |
273: |---|---|---|
274: | **Hook entry point** (`repo-memory hook <harness> <event>`) | Deterministic delivery; spool writing (§7, §6.2). No processes, network, LLM or job-table writes. | Event path |
275: | **Tick** (`repo-memory tick`) | Spool ingestion, the job table, sweep, git checks, housekeeping runs, reports, calendar jobs | Antigravity scheduled sidecar; OS scheduler; CLI (`repo-memory run` is an alias) |
276: | **Entity extractor** | Builds the code skeleton (subsystems, files, symbols, config keys, topics, tools, error strings). No LLM. | Tick, when HEAD or configuration changes |
277: | **Pipeline stages 1–6** | Turn events into claims and views (§6) | Tick |
278: | **Re-check scheduler** | Queues claims for re-verification when their dependencies change (§8) | Tick, from spooled `PostToolUse` events and its own hash checks |
279: | **Pull tools** | `memory.ask`, `memory.why`, `memory.history`, `memory.brief`, `memory.note`, `memory.stats`. Exposed by a stdio MCP server that reads the SQLite index; `ask` and `brief` may make one synchronous housekeeping run. | Spawned by the harness per session |
280: | **Review surface** | Weekly review report (IDE) and the batched memory PR (git host) | Tick |
281: 
282: Processes communicate only through files and SQLite in WAL mode. There is no socket, no long-running process and nothing detached. Everything works on macOS, Linux and Windows.
283:

285: - Hooks behave the same.

- [x] Capture health metrics: sessions seen, captured, skipped, missed.

## Completion Report
<!-- Written by the worker at task completion -->

### Status
Complete

### Changes Made
- Implemented `internal/core/metrics/types.go` containing:
  - Base record model (`Record`, `BaseRecord`, `MetricType`).
  - `CaptureHealth` capturing sessions seen, captured, skipped (with skip reasons like recursion guard), missed (transcript gone before sweep), and capture rate.
  - `HookExecution` capturing hook execution latency and cumulative session execution time.
  - `TickHealth` capturing scheduled tick duration, budget exhaustion, skipped overlaps, backlog maps, sessions caught by sweep, and spool-to-delivery latency.
  - `BudgetExhaustion` recording stage, token/run/time limits vs consumption, exhaustion status, and reason.
  - `TranscriptMeasurement` recording transcript footprint, token estimation, tool traffic breakdown, compaction ratio, and truncation expansion ratio.
- Implemented `internal/core/metrics/writer.go` providing thread-safe JSONL appending under `<data-dir>/<repo-id>/metrics/*.jsonl` with daily file rotation (`YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl`), fixed file overrides (`WithFileName`), forced flush/sync options (`WithSyncOnWrite`), and arbitrary `io.Writer` targets (`NewWriterFromIO`).
- Implemented `internal/core/metrics/reader.go` providing structured JSONL deserialization, stream seeking, and telemetry aggregators:
  - `AggregateCaptureHealth` for overall seen/captured/skipped/missed counts, reason breakdowns, and capture rate.
  - `AggregateHookExecutions` for p50, p95, p99, mean, min, max percentiles per event type, and session cumulative latencies.
  - `AggregateTickHealth` for tick execution stats, backlog averages, and spool-to-delivery latencies.
  - `AggregateBudgetExhaustion` for stage-specific exhaustion counts and token consumption totals.
- Implemented `internal/core/metrics/measure.go` providing transcript size and compaction measurement tools:
  - `OpenTranscriptStream` following §6.2 priority order: `transcript_full.jsonl`, chunked transcripts concatenated in lexical order (`chunks/transcript_full/*.jsonl`), or compact fallback (`transcript.jsonl`).
  - `MeasureTranscript` normalizing steps, detecting tool traffic (both tool calls and output responses), and applying `compact.NewCompactor().Compact()` to compute kept characters and compaction ratios.
  - `MeasureDirectories` and `FormatSection441Table` producing markdown comparison tables.
- Added comprehensive unit and integration test suites:
  - `writer_test.go`: File persistence, daily rotation, in-memory IO, reader roundtrip, and race-free concurrent writes (25 goroutines x 40 writes).
  - `health_test.go`: Capture health tracking, hook percentile distributions (p50/p95/p99), tick execution health, and budget exhaustion assertions.
  - `measure_test.go`: Fixture validation (`full_normal`, `full_chunked`, `compact`), synthetic compaction test confirming compaction ratio >= 4x, and live re-measurement on surviving full transcripts (`~/.gemini/antigravity/brain`).

### Decisions Made
- Standardized token estimation at 4 characters per token (`chars / 4`) across raw transcript text, tool traffic, and compacted outputs.
- In Antigravity transcripts, tool traffic is accurately captured by including both tool call payloads (`tool_calls`) and subsequent tool response steps (type `GENERIC` / `TOOL_OUTPUT` / `COMMAND_OUTPUT` following a tool call), yielding 77%–83% tool traffic on real transcripts (matching §4.4.1's 86%–90%).
- Full transcripts were measured against surviving conversations on disk:
  - Median tokens: 56k (top-level: 50k tokens, subagent: 68k tokens)
  - Mean tokens: 71k
  - Tool traffic: 78%
  - Compaction ratio: 5.4x (exceeding the PR-02a exit criterion target of >= 4x).
- Preserved strict boundary rules: `internal/core/metrics` does not import any concrete harness adapter (`antigravity`, `claudecode`, or `fake` in production code).

### Dead Ends & Warnings
- When using `io.Reader` sources with `Reader`, streams must implement `io.Seeker` or use separate readers if multiple scan passes (`ReadCaptureHealth`, `ReadHookExecutions`, etc.) are made against the same input stream. `reader.go` was updated to automatically seek to offset 0 when an `io.Seeker` is detected.

### Out-of-Scope Findings
(none)

### Blockers
(none)
